title: Functional Components
description: Understand functional components, the modern way to build React components.

data.text: **Functional components** are JavaScript functions that return JSX. Since React 16.8 introduced Hooks, functional components can manage state, handle side effects, and do everything class components can — with less code.

React originally supported class components. Functional components existed but were called 'stateless' because they could not hold state. Hooks changed that. Today, functional components are the recommended default.

data.title: Benefits
items: Easier to read and test because they are plain functions
Hooks let you reuse stateful logic without wrappers

data.text: A functional component is simply a function that returns JSX. By convention, the function name starts with a capital letter so React knows it is a component, not a built-in HTML tag.

data.title: Basic Functional Component
Capitalization Matters
data.text: HTML tags like div and span are lowercase. Custom components must start with an uppercase letter, otherwise React treats them as built-in tags.
Exporting a component lets other files import and use it. Use a default export when a file contains one main component. Use named exports when a file contains multiple related components.

data.title: Export Patterns

data.text: Keep components in a dedicated `src/components/` folder. Name the file after the component so teammates can find files quickly.

data.title: Project Structure
data.code:
src/
├── components/
│   ├── Button.jsx

data.text: Components accept inputs called props. In the next lesson you will learn how to pass data from parent to child components.

data.title: Using Props

data.title: Exercise: Build a Greeting Card
data.description: Create a component that accepts a name prop and displays a personalized greeting.
steps: Create a new file GreetingCard.jsx inside src/components.
Accept a name prop in the function parameters.
Return JSX with a greeting message that includes the name.
Import and render it in App.jsx with two different names.
data.expectedOutcome: A reusable GreetingCard component rendered twice with different names.

items.question: Are class components still supported?
items.answer: Yes, but they are legacy. React 19 still supports them, but all new features target functional components and hooks.

items.question: Can I use TypeScript with functional components?
items.answer: Yes. TypeScript integrates cleanly with function components. Define props as an interface or type and annotate the function parameter.

items.question: Should I always use default exports?
items.answer: Prefer named exports for better refactoring and auto-import support in editors. Use default exports only for the main component of a file.

items.question: What is the difference between export and export default?
items.answer: `export default` exports a single value and is imported without braces. `export` creates named exports imported with braces.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Functional components are functions that return JSX.
Component names must start with a capital letter.
Export components to use them in other files.
Prefer named exports for better editor tooling.
data.takeaway: You can now create and export functional components. Next, you will learn how to pass data into them using props.
